title: A drawn path's outline settings read like the icon drawing mock's Stroke section
goal: The icon drawing mock gives a picked glyph a Stroke section with Width, Caps and Align. The app shows the same settings under the Outline row with different names and controls: Thickness as a slider where the mock has Width as a dropdown of weights, and Ends as three pictures where the mock has Caps as the words Butt, Round and Square. Bring the path outline settings to the mock, or ask the user where the app's shared words (Thickness, Ends, used by lines and arrows too) should win.
notes: Found while building the Align row (task a-drawn-path-takes-an-outline-inside-centred-or, 2026-10-08). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-draw-wt.html ~line 411 (#secStroke: Width select reading 1.75, Caps seg Butt/Round/Square with Round on, Align select Center). App: Sources/Photonz/ShapePartSettings.swift .stroke slot (thickness slider labelled Thickness) and Sources/Photonz/PathLineStylePickers.swift (Pattern, Ends, Corners picture segments, Align dropdown). Ends is hidden on a closed solid path by design (PathContent.showsLineEnds) while the mock always shows Caps. Thickness and Ends are the words lines and arrows use too, so renaming for paths alone splits the vocabulary: that is a card for the user, not a runner guess. Pattern and Corners go further than the mock and are not differences.
acceptance: A picked closed path's outline settings are compared side by side with the Stroke section of icon-draw-wt.html, and every difference is fixed or carried by a decision card
If the mock's words win, Width and Caps read the same for a drawn path as the mock draws them, and walks that expect Thickness or Ends on a path are updated in the same commit
A walk at Next defaults photographs the result and an audit sits beside the mock
